name: PA-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: Incumbent Brendan Boyle's large financial advantage ($5.6M cash on hand)
No polling and minimal outside spending signal a low-attention race
Prediction markets price Boyle near certain to win
model.rationale: Boyle holds a heavily Democratic Philadelphia-area seat, a dominant fundraising edge, and no serious outside opposition, while markets price his win probability near 97%. With no polls or expert ratings to contradict the fundamentals, the race stays firmly in Safe D territory.
model.watch: A surprise scandal or an unexpectedly well-funded Republican challenger could tighten the race, though the district's lean makes an upset very unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Brendan Boyle is seeking another term in a Philadelphia-area district that leans about 19 points Democratic, making it one of the safest Democratic House seats in Pennsylvania. He enters the general election with roughly $5.6 million on hand after raising about $2.5 million, while Republican Jessica Arriaga reports minimal disclosed fundraising and no outside spending has materialized on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, Boyle's incumbency, and his financial dominance. Prediction markets price Boyle's chances near 97 percent. The expected margin is about 25 points, with the seat firmly in the Safe D category.
